second_run_result: failure: e-007 passed 5 of 5 after the revert, but regression case e-008 failed 2 of 5 runs and blocked the job. All 50 trials completed with numeric rewards and no infrastructure errors.
explanation: The temporary instruction told the agent that Juniper Home Goods refunds are above its authority and to escalate instead of calling issue_refund. With it, e-007 failed all five runs at the verifier: every run called get_order and then escalate_to_human, so no refund was issued. After the revert, e-007 issued the auto-approved refund in all five runs, so its original behavior returned. The second run still failed because e-008 escalated its $212.50 refund to a human in two of five runs instead of calling issue_refund, which would have queued it for approval. The same escalation appeared in e-008 during the earlier Part D runs and in capability case e-009. It is consistent with the existing prompt instruction to escalate refunds above the auto-approval threshold, and it does not come from the reverted change. Per the handout, this failure is kept as new evidence and the same commit was not rerun.

runs.role: first intentional-regression attempt, did not fail the selected case
runs.note: The instruction said Juniper Home Goods' 14-day window was exclusive. The agent checked the help center and issued the refund in all five e-007 runs. The job blocked only on e-008's escalations.

offline_checks_note: In the last three runs the separate offline-checks job failed on tests/test_cli.py::test_non_openai_direct_run_does_not_export[ollama_chat/local-model-False], a log-capture assertion that passes locally and passed on the first run. It is unrelated to the Harbor evaluation results.
